claims.text: The deviation is established on the figure that governs. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test; the trace reads 30.16 km against a booked optimal of 23.2 km, an excess of 6.96 km. That is 30.0% of optimal, so both establishment gates pass at once — above 20% of optimal and above 0.8 km in absolute terms.

Nothing impairs that measurement. The trace samples every 10 seconds at 100.0% coverage, has no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds, so none of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires. The deviation may therefore rest on the gps_trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

The rider's initial burden is discharged. POL-RD-08(a) is met because trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-03207 with the recorded pickup, start and end timestamps in sequence, and POL-RD-08(b) is met by the 6.96 km excess measured from an unimpaired trace, so the burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The rider carries no history that raises the corroboration bar POL-RD-08 sets: on the citable field rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d the figure is 0, so the 'excess below 30%' corroboration rule is not engaged on this claim.

The refund is then arithmetic, not discretionary. The trip is METERED and the multiplier is 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier. Charged total is 38.25. Recomputed against the booked optimal route: 3.80 base + 0.75 x 23.2 km + 0.28 x 31.3 min = 29.964, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no fixed surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo discount, giving a recomputed fare of 30.764. Charged less recomputed is 7.486, and the payable figure rounds UP to 7.50. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share of 38.25.

The driver's only answer is the chat line 'can we stop at Jurong Point first'. I do not dispute the message is on the record, but POL-RD-04 exonerates only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor' attributable to the instruction, and not one derived fact in this bundle identifies those leave and rejoin points or measures the distance between them. The only derived fact about the waypoint is proximity — the nearest fix is 49.5 m away — which shows the vehicle passed near Jurong Point and says nothing about how much of the 6.96 km that cost. The driver's counterparty statement cites no evidence ID and no clause, so under POL-RD-08 it is discarded, and even if his reference to the chat is read as pointing to EV-CHAT-03207, the exoneration remains unquantified on this record and cannot reduce the POL-RD-02 figure.

No external-cause explanation is available to displace the measured excess. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-03207-01, is MISSING — weight 0.0, no payload, no advisory covering the Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 corridor in this window — so no road-closure exoneration under POL-RD-03 can be run, and the driver has not asserted a traffic cause in any event. The excess stands as measured.

Nothing else moves the money: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and zero ERP, so there is no off-route pass-through correction to add or subtract under POL-RD-09, and the 7.50 refund computed under POL-RD-02 is the whole of the monetary movement on this trip.

claims.text: The rider asked for this detour in the app. MSG-03207-001, sent by the RIDER at 11:55:13 — 60 seconds after the meter started at 11:54:13 — reads 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', and the driver agreed 20 seconds later. The instruction therefore comes from the rider, is timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor (no artifact places the corridor exit earlier; the requested waypoint was not reached until 12:14:03) and in any event falls well inside POL-RD-04(b)'s three-minute after-window, and it names a place specifically enough to act on. POL-RD-04(a) to (c) are met.

The corroboration POL-RD-04 demands is satisfied on the very field the clause names. chat_message.waypoint_hint for MSG-03207-001 resolves on the platform's own ingest to 1.237339, 103.736859 ('Jurong Point'), and the driver's trace passes 49.5 m from that point at 12:14:03 — well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m threshold, and the platform flags it within_threshold true. This is a field comparison, not an act of geocoding, and it succeeds.

Because the detour was rider-requested, the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, and materiality is assessed on the excess that REMAINS. The measured excess is 6.96 km, or 30.0% of the 23.2 km optimal; the POL-RD-01 establishment gate therefore requires more than 4.64 km remaining (20% of 23.2 km). The record identifies exactly one off-corridor destination — the rider's Jurong Point stop, which the trace confirms the vehicle actually reached — and no other cause of off-corridor travel appears anywhere in the bundle. Once that requested detour is excluded, no excess meeting the POL-RD-01 gate survives and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

The burden POL-RD-08 places on the driver is discharged, and discharged in the form that clause demands: a specific artifact and a specific clause. The artifact is EV-CHAT-03207, the chat log; the clause is POL-RD-04, rider-requested detour. The very artifact the rider needs in order to complain of the stop is the artifact that records the rider asking for it, and the driver's counterparty statement on file says the same thing.

POL-RD-14 does not defeat that reliance. That clause is confined to a rider instruction the trace does NOT corroborate — the vehicle never coming within 200 m of the waypoint. Here the trace comes within 49.5 m of the requested waypoint, inside POL-RD-04's 200 m threshold, so the instruction is corroborated, it is the cause of the measured off-corridor travel, and it is excluded under POL-RD-04 rather than set aside under POL-RD-14.

The trace this argument rests on is clean, so the corroboration drawn from it is reliable. It is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 237 fixes at a 10 second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. It is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no POL-GEN-02 discount attaches to it, and the 49.5 m waypoint approach computed from it is a real measurement rather than an artefact of a broken trace.

No repeat-deviation uplift applies on this trip. The deviation is established but not MATERIAL — 6.96 km is under the 8.0 km material threshold and 30.0% is under the 50% material threshold — so POL-RD-06 is not even engaged by this trip. Even if it were, the pattern test fails on the only fields the clause permits: deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 228 is 0.004, far below 0.05. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follows, and no other profile field may be used for that test.

There is nothing left for a pass-through correction to operate on. The fare ledger carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge: erp_gantries is empty, the off-route ERP total is 0.00 and the on-route ERP total is 0.00, and this trip neither originates at an airport nor carries a fixed surcharge line. No POL-RD-09 correction is due, and there is no billing-integrity defect to refer.

The chat log is complete and untruncated and contains exactly the two messages quoted above; nothing in it objects to the route at any point during the trip, and the friend named in the claim filed no statement in this bundle. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence id carries no weight, so a witness who is named but never recorded adds nothing to the rider's case.

NO_ACTION is the outcome that simply leaves the fare as the platform has already settled it: EV-FARE-03207 records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. On this rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION preserves that state, which is the correct result once the rider-requested detour is excluded — the rider pays for the trip the rider asked for.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — decision on dispute DSP-03207 (trip TRP-03207).

THE MEASUREMENT. The GPS trace EV-GPS-03207 measures 30.16 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off; the booked optimal route on the trip record (EV-TRIP-03207) is 23.2 km. The excess is 6.96 km, 30.0% of optimal — above both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km), so a route deviation is established, and I accept the rider's evidence on that point. The trace is clean: 237 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no POL-GEN-02 discount attaches, and it needs no independent corroboration.

WHY NO REFUND FOLLOWS. The rider's own in-app message, MSG-03207-001 (EV-CHAT-03207), sent at 11:55:13 — 60 seconds after the meter started at 11:54:13 and before the vehicle left the optimal corridor — reads 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', and the driver agreed at 11:55:33. Under POL-RD-04 the instruction (a) comes from the rider, (b) is timed before the corridor exit and in any event well inside the three-minute window, and (c) names a place specifically enough to act on — it is the clause's own example. The corroboration POL-RD-04 demands is satisfied on the field it names: the platform resolved the message's waypoint_hint to Jurong Point (1.237339, 103.736859) and the driver's trace passes 49.5 m from that point at 12:14:03, flagged within_threshold true and far inside the 200 m test. POL-RD-14 does not set that aside, because the trace corroborates the instruction rather than failing it.

WHAT IS EXCLUDED. POL-RD-04 excludes 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor'. On this bundle the Jurong Point stop is the only off-corridor excursion: the trace confirms the vehicle reached the waypoint, and nothing in the bundle shows any second excursion. The friend named in the claim filed no statement, and the claim's 'not a tour' cites no evidence id, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight. The measured excess is therefore the excess attributable to the one rider-requested detour; excluding it leaves nothing above the POL-RD-01 gate (20% of 23.2 km = 4.64 km) and no deviation survives.

THE 7.50 THE RIDER ASKED FOR. The rider's arithmetic — charged total 38.25 less a recomputed fare of 30.764, a refund of 7.50 — is correct in itself, but POL-RD-04 excuses the excess before POL-RD-02 runs: the rider asked for the stop, so the rider pays for the trip the rider asked for. The driver's submission that the whole excess is the requested detour is accepted; the rider's submission that the exoneration cannot be applied because no leave-and-rejoin distance is stated is rejected, because with a single requested off-corridor stop the measured excess is that distance. The driver's counterparty statement (which cites no evidence id and no clause) is not relied on; the finding rests on EV-CHAT-03207 and EV-GPS-03207.

NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires the rider to have been billed for less distance than the trace records, by more than 1.0 km. The fare ledger charged 30.2 km and the trace records 30.16 km, so there is no unbilled distance and nothing is owed to the driver.

NO REFERRAL. The deviation is not material (6.96 km is under the 8.0 km line and 30.0% is under 50%), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and in any event its pattern test fails on the only fields it permits — deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1 of 228 completed trips is 0.004 (below 0.05). No POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises: the fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and no surcharge (erp_gantries empty; off-route and on-route ERP both 0.00). The bundle's traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03207-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but no party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-13 are not in play.

RESULT. NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays 0.00. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. The monetary effect is nil, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05. If the rider can produce record-type evidence that the vehicle travelled off the optimal corridor somewhere other than the Jurong Point stop, that would reopen the attribution on appeal.

Both parties: I have decided trip TRP-03207 (pickup Blk 640 Jurong West St 61, drop-off Blk 130 Bukit Batok West Ave 6). The outcome is NO_ACTION — the fare stands as charged, because the extra distance is the distance the rider asked the driver to drive.

The measurement. Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km on EV-GPS-03207, which reads 30.16 km, against the booked optimal of 23.2 km on EV-TRIP-03207 — an excess of 6.96 km, or 30.0% of optimal. That clears both establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is established on the trace; it is not a MATERIAL deviation (under 50% and under 8.0 km).

The rider asked for the detour. EV-CHAT-03207 records the rider's message MSG-03207-001 at 11:55:13, one minute after the meter started: 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', carrying the platform-resolved waypoint_hint (1.237339, 103.736859). The driver replied 'ok' at 11:55:33. The instruction therefore comes from the rider, was sent before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and names a place specifically enough to act on — POL-RD-04(a) to (c) all hold. The gps_trace corroborates it: the driver's trace passes 49.5 m from that waypoint at 12:14:03, well inside the clause's 200 m test, and the platform records within_threshold true. POL-RD-04 therefore applies to this trip.

Effect. POL-RD-04 excludes the excess distance attributable to the rider's requested stop before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. The only off-corridor destination anywhere in the bundle is Jurong Point — the stop the rider asked for — and the trace confirms the vehicle reached it; no other off-corridor travel appears anywhere. Excluding that requested detour leaves no excess meeting the POL-RD-01 gate, and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

The rider's answers. I have considered the argument that no derived fact identifies the leave/rejoin points or measures the detour's distance, so the exoneration cannot be quantified and 7.50 (charged_total 38.25 less recomputed_fare 30.764) should still be refunded. The clause excludes the excess attributable to the instruction; the record shows a single off-corridor excursion — the stop the rider requested — and the rider identifies no other off-corridor cause to which any of the 6.96 km could be assigned. The absence of a separate derived field creates no residual where the sole cause is identified. POL-RD-14 does not rescue the rider either: it governs the case where the trace does NOT corroborate the instruction, and here it does (49.5 m). POL-RD-10(7) is not engaged: a request that was made and a route that followed it are consistent, not contradictory.

Other money. There are no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge (erp_gantries empty; off-route and on-route ERP both 0.00), so no POL-RD-09 correction arises. The rider was billed distance_charged_km 30.2 km against a trace of 30.16 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall and no POL-RD-04 DRIVER_COMPENSATION is due. No POL-RD-06 uplift or driver-conduct referral: there is no material deviation, and on the only citable fields deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1 over completed_trips_90d 228 is 0.004 (below 0.05); no other profile field was used for that test. The witness named in the claim filed no statement, so adds nothing (POL-RD-08). The driver's counterparty statement ('The rider asked for the stop, it is in the chat') is consistent with the record but carries no weight of its own; the exoneration does not depend on it.

Status and route. NO_ACTION leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 as they stand (POL-GEN-03). The monetary effect is nil, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so the ruling executes on issue. Confidence is 0.85, above the 0.70 floor; the facts this ruling rests on are carried by complete artifacts, EV-CHAT-03207 and EV-GPS-03207, each at weight 1.0, so no discount and no POL-GEN-02 escalation applies. Either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the fare for TRP-03207 stands as charged. No refund and no driver compensation is due.

What the record measures. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-03207) reads 30.16 km against a booked optimal of 23.2 km (EV-TRIP-03207) — an excess of 6.96 km, or 30.0%. Both POL-RD-01 gates are crossed (over 20% and over 0.8 km), and the trace is clean: 237 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps. Nothing impairs it under POL-RD-07(a)–(c), so the deviation is established as measured.

Why the driver is not charged for it. The chat log (EV-CHAT-03207) carries the rider's own message MSG-03207-001, sent at 11:55:13 — one minute after the meter started — reading 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', and the driver's 'ok' 20 seconds later. POL-RD-04's three conditions are met: the instruction came from the rider; it was given before the vehicle left the optimal corridor (and in any event well inside the three-minute after-window); and it names a place specifically enough to act on. The clause's corroboration test is met on the clause's own field: chat_message.waypoint_hint for that message resolves to the point the trace passes 49.5 m from at 12:14:03, inside the 200 m threshold. POL-RD-14 does not assist the rider here — it governs the case where the trace never comes within 200 m of the waypoint, and this trace does.

On your point, rider, that nothing in the bundle identifies the points where the vehicle left and rejoined the optimal corridor: it is noted, but it does not carry. The record identifies exactly one off-corridor destination — the Jurong Point stop the trace confirms the vehicle reached — and nothing else in the bundle accounts for off-corridor travel: no traffic advisory (the only one, EV-ADVIS-03207-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no fact), no ERP gantry, no second waypoint. The trace's farthest fix from the start is 18.56 km, at the drop-off, so there is no independent outward wandering beyond the requested stop. On that record the whole of the 6.96 km excess is attributable to the rider-requested detour and is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. With it excluded, no excess survives the POL-RD-01 gate and there is nothing for POL-RD-02 to refund. For completeness, had the deviation stood, POL-RD-02 on EV-FARE-03207 would have given charged_total 38.25 less a recomputed fare of 30.764 (3.80 base + 0.75 × 23.2 km + 0.28 × 31.3 min, × the surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, + 0.80 platform fee) = 7.486, rounded up to 7.50; that figure is not payable because the deviation it depends on is exonerated.

Nothing else moves the money. EV-FARE-03207 carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge, so no POL-RD-09 pass-through correction and no billing-integrity referral arises. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: the excess is not material (6.96 km is under 8.0 km and 30.0% under 50%), and on the only citable profile fields driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (under 3) and 1 over 228 completed trips is 0.004 (under 0.05), so there is no repeat-pattern uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The friend named in the claim filed no statement in this bundle and her account cites no evidence id, so under POL-RD-08 it adds nothing. The driver's counterparty statement agrees with the chat but carries no weight and is not relied on.

Every artifact this ruling rests on — the chat log, the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — is at full weight 1.0, so nothing is discounted; the one impaired artifact (EV-ADVIS-03207-01, MISSING, weight 0.0) carries no fact. The fare is left as settled: payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
This dispute concerns trip TRP-03207, Jurong West to Bukit Batok West, and it turns on why the trip ran long. The measurement itself is not in doubt. POL-RD-01 makes the trace the governing figure, and the trace reads 30.16 km against a booked optimal of 23.2 km — an excess of 6.96 km, or 30.0% (EV-GPS-03207, EV-TRIP-03207). The trace is clean: 237 fixes at 10-second spacing, 100.0% coverage, a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds and no gaps, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no POL-GEN-02 discount attaches to it, and the deviation cannot be defeated on trace-quality grounds.

But the excess is explained by the stop the rider asked for. At 11:55:13, one minute after the meter started, the rider sent 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something' (EV-CHAT-03207, MSG-03207-001), and the driver agreed 20 seconds later. The platform resolved that message's waypoint_hint to 1.237339, 103.736859, and the driver's trace passes 49.5 m from that point at 12:14:03 — inside the 200 m test POL-RD-04 sets. The instruction comes from the rider, is timestamped within the window POL-RD-04(b) allows, and names a place specifically enough to act on. Under POL-RD-04 the excess attributable to a rider-requested stop is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, and the trace corroborates the instruction, so POL-RD-14 — which governs only an instruction the trace does NOT corroborate — does not apply here, and neither does the POL-RD-10(7) contradiction it confines.

The rider argues that no field in the bundle measures the distance between the point where the vehicle left the optimal corridor and the point where it rejoined, so the exoneration is unquantified and the full excess must stand. That argument does not change the result. The trace shows a single off-corridor destination — the Jurong Point stop — and no other cause of off-corridor travel appears anywhere in the bundle. Once that requested stop is set aside, no excess meeting POL-RD-01's gate (more than 20% of 23.2 km, that is more than 4.64 km, and more than 0.8 km absolute) survives. The deviation is therefore not established on this trip, and the rider's own claim that a vehicle cannot reach a waypoint roughly 12 km off the corridor and back within a 2.32 km margin is not one the record supports.

Because no deviation survives, the fare recomputation under POL-RD-02 does not run. For transparency I record what the arithmetic would have produced: charged_total 38.25 against a recomputed fare of 30.764, a difference of 7.486 rounded up to 7.50 (EV-FARE-03207). That figure is not payable, and the surge multiplier of 1.0 was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier. There is no ERP or toll line and no airport surcharge on the ledger — erp_gantries is empty and both on-route and off-route ERP totals are 0.00 — so no standalone pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 is due, and there is no billing-integrity line to refer. The driver's 90-day deviation record (deviation_flags_90d 1 of completed_trips_90d 228, a rate of 0.004) is far below POL-RD-06's threshold of 3 flags or 0.05, and the deviation was not MATERIAL (6.96 km under 8.0 km; 30.0% under 50%), so no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral arises. No traffic cause was asserted, and the absent advisory (EV-ADVIS-03207-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) therefore plays no part.

The outcome is NO_ACTION: the fare stands as the platform settled it, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 (EV-FARE-03207). The friend the rider named filed no statement in this bundle, and a witness who is named but never recorded adds nothing under POL-RD-08. The driver's own counterparty statement cites no evidence ID and is on that footing discarded as an unsupported assertion; the exoneration rests on the chat log and the trace, not on the statement. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fired, and the monetary effect is nil. Either party may appeal this provisional ruling once, within 30 days, under POL-GEN-04.

No external-cause explanation is available to displace the measured excess. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-03207-01, is MISSING — weight 0.0, no payload, no advisory covering the Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 corridor in this window — so no road-closure exoneration under POL-RD-03 can be run, and the driver has not asserted a traffic cause in any event. The excess stands as measured.

ledger.claim: Nothing else moves the money: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and zero ERP, so there is no off-route pass-through correction to add or subtract under POL-RD-09, and the 7.50 refund computed under POL-RD-02 is the whole of the monetary movement on this trip.

The rider asked for this detour in the app. MSG-03207-001, sent by the RIDER at 11:55:13 — 60 seconds after the meter started at 11:54:13 — reads 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', and the driver agreed 20 seconds later. The instruction therefore comes from the rider, is timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor (no artifact places the corridor exit earlier; the requested waypoint was not reached until 12:14:03) and in any event falls well inside POL-RD-04(b)'s three-minute after-window, and it names a place specifically enough to act on. POL-RD-04(a) to (c) are met.

The corroboration POL-RD-04 demands is satisfied on the very field the clause names. chat_message.waypoint_hint for MSG-03207-001 resolves on the platform's own ingest to 1.237339, 103.736859 ('Jurong Point'), and the driver's trace passes 49.5 m from that point at 12:14:03 — well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m threshold, and the platform flags it within_threshold true. This is a field comparison, not an act of geocoding, and it succeeds.

Because the detour was rider-requested, the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, and materiality is assessed on the excess that REMAINS. The measured excess is 6.96 km, or 30.0% of the 23.2 km optimal; the POL-RD-01 establishment gate therefore requires more than 4.64 km remaining (20% of 23.2 km). The record identifies exactly one off-corridor destination — the rider's Jurong Point stop, which the trace confirms the vehicle actually reached — and no other cause of off-corridor travel appears anywhere in the bundle. Once that requested detour is excluded, no excess meeting the POL-RD-01 gate survives and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

The burden POL-RD-08 places on the driver is discharged, and discharged in the form that clause demands: a specific artifact and a specific clause. The artifact is EV-CHAT-03207, the chat log; the clause is POL-RD-04, rider-requested detour. The very artifact the rider needs in order to complain of the stop is the artifact that records the rider asking for it, and the driver's counterparty statement on file says the same thing.

POL-RD-14 does not defeat that reliance. That clause is confined to a rider instruction the trace does NOT corroborate — the vehicle never coming within 200 m of the waypoint. Here the trace comes within 49.5 m of the requested waypoint, inside POL-RD-04's 200 m threshold, so the instruction is corroborated, it is the cause of the measured off-corridor travel, and it is excluded under POL-RD-04 rather than set aside under POL-RD-14.

The trace this argument rests on is clean, so the corroboration drawn from it is reliable. It is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 237 fixes at a 10 second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. It is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no POL-GEN-02 discount attaches to it, and the 49.5 m waypoint approach computed from it is a real measurement rather than an artefact of a broken trace.

No repeat-deviation uplift applies on this trip. The deviation is established but not MATERIAL — 6.96 km is under the 8.0 km material threshold and 30.0% is under the 50% material threshold — so POL-RD-06 is not even engaged by this trip. Even if it were, the pattern test fails on the only fields the clause permits: deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 228 is 0.004, far below 0.05. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follows, and no other profile field may be used for that test.

There is nothing left for a pass-through correction to operate on. The fare ledger carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge: erp_gantries is empty, the off-route ERP total is 0.00 and the on-route ERP total is 0.00, and this trip neither originates at an airport nor carries a fixed surcharge line. No POL-RD-09 correction is due, and there is no billing-integrity defect to refer.

The chat log is complete and untruncated and contains exactly the two messages quoted above; nothing in it objects to the route at any point during the trip, and the friend named in the claim filed no statement in this bundle. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence id carries no weight, so a witness who is named but never recorded adds nothing to the rider's case.

NO_ACTION is the outcome that simply leaves the fare as the platform has already settled it: EV-FARE-03207 records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. On this rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION preserves that state, which is the correct result once the rider-requested detour is excluded — the rider pays for the trip the rider asked for.
